add.text:
Read this numbered, cleaned transcript of the owner talking. Turn it into an outline a reader
takes in at a glance: "tangible, familiar, easy to digest". The owner's words for it: "putting
familiar names, like the headings" on the thing being discussed and on each of its parts.

Output Markdown in EXACTLY this shape:

# <the concrete thing being discussed>
## <a familiar name for one part of it>
- <one point, in the owner's own words> [S#, S#]
  - <a detail or example of that point, only if it needs its own line> [S#]
## <the next part>
- <...> [S#]

Rules:
- The H1 is CONCRETE: a thing a reader could point at — a class, a page, a tab, a tool, a feature
  (the owner's example: "Page class"). Never an abstract category like "AI processes", "Thoughts"
  or "Feedback". If the transcript covers several separate things, name them plainly in the one
  H1 ("Page class and Sidebar") and give each its own H2 or H2s.
- Exactly ONE "#" H1. One "##" H2 per distinct part — never invent one just to have more.
- Each H2 is a FAMILIAR name a reader already knows. If a name already exists for that part (the
  owner's example: "Layout"), use that exact name; otherwise use the owner's own word for it.
- ONE BULLET PER POINT, NOT PER SENTENCE. When several sentences make one point (a claim, its
  reason, "so I like that"), merge them into one bullet, a short line in the owner's own words,
  citing every one of those sentences. Filler that makes no point of its own ("Couple of things.")
  gets no bullet: add its number to the nearest bullet's citation instead.
- AT MOST TWO LEVELS: a bullet, and sub-bullets under it. Never a third level.
- KEEP EVERY POINT. Merging sentences that make the same point is required; dropping a point is
  not allowed. Never turn a hedge ("maybe", "I think", "I guess") into a flat claim.
- Cite EVERY sentence number EXACTLY ONCE, in the one bullet where its main point went — never
  under two headings. Form: [S3, S7], each number individually, never a range like [S6-S9]. Use
  only numbers that appear below.

STYLE of anything the owner will read (the owner's rules):
- It is an OVERVIEW of what was said, in the owner's own key words. Never the whole rant, never a retelling.
- Each point has its answer or action baked in: say what is done, what to do, or what is still open. Do not invent an answer the transcript or the facts do not give; mark such a point open instead.
- Order by dependency and ease: clarifications and quick items first, then what depends on them. If neither applies, keep the owner's order.
- Reuse the same names for the same things every time, so they become familiar, and always name the context (the page, class, module or session) a point belongs to.
- Headings are big: "#" for the one subject, "##" for each part, "###" only when a part truly needs a split. Never "####" or smaller. Every heading starts with one fitting emoji icon.
- Under a heading: short titled lists. A status bullet starts with ✅ (done) or ⬜ (not done) when the status is known; otherwise a plain "-" bullet. Few emoji, never decoration.
- Every card cites the clean-sentence numbers it came from, like [S3, S7], each number individually.
Apply this to the headings and bullets of the outline.

Cleaned transcript:
"""
S1. They don't have to be too big on those targets, but, well, yeah, I mean, it's mainly play and pause.
S2. The rewind 10 seconds button could be useful per card.
S3. Also, I was kind of thinking that if you... tap, but you could tap somewhere on the text and that could rewind to that spot in the text.
S4. I'm not sure if that's, well, because otherwise, if you have a giant paragraph and you get halfway through it and the only option is to restart it or nothing.
S5. I'm not sure how granular we would want those click events to be able to reactivate a specific threshold.
S6. And then I'm not sure if that needs to regenerate anything or if the UI can handle all of that by itself.
S7. I don't know, those are all things worth exploring.
S8. I don't know if any one of those is absolutely necessary.
S9. Seems like it's working pretty well, but I'd say the biggest thing that we want to fix is unifying V2 and V3, and that's really about... getting the chat and messages systems to work more coherently.
S10. And a big part of that is making sure that we're handling the, well, yeah, the data structures, the streaming of the text and transcripts, the frequency of processing those transcripts.
S11. I think they, right now, the, this big wall of text problem doesn't solve the.
S12. Well, it's basically like the transcribe mode or the remote control mode on a VS Code tab.
S13. It works, but because I have to transcribe, well, I tend to transcribe large chunks in that mode rather than sending it frequently.
S14. And so in this mode, I have to do a long pause before it gets sent off.
S15. And right now you have a tendency once I pause to automatically respond.
S16. And so continuing to transcribe then becomes kind of a pain because you end up interrupting me.
S17. And then when you interrupt me, I didn't know you were going to talk, so that then I keep transcribing, and then my new transcription interrupts you.
S18. And so then you never read aloud the long response that you created.
S19. And I don't think right now I have a way to replay any of them, like if I click on them it doesn't do anything.
S20. So that could be probably one of the more useful things.
S21. Another interesting question is does the audio that gets generated get lost, like do we just delete it, or are we saving it in a way where on reload, we could go back and replay all of them without having to use the server to regenerate them.
S22. I'm not sure if that's useful.
S23. That would mean saving a ton of audio.
S24. However, alternative is to just regenerate it and play it back again, which also could be just as easily easy, and if not better.
S25. So then the audio just becomes a temporary thing rather than a saved thing.
S26. Yeah, a lot of different questions to ask and answer, and probably explore via the settings or whatever.
S27. But I'm glad we got voice working.
S28. I think it's pretty cool.
S29. And lastly, what I was going to say is if we can send my transcriptions per sentence to either a fast or smartest...
S30. And by the way, that green checkmark seems to be a little bit out of sync with the brain icon.
S31. And so looking into those and how they're triggered, well, I'm not sure if... I think we might still have a fast assistant running on this session who's processing everything that I say.
S32. Yeah, and the idea before was that the fast assistant would get even comma level punctuation, periods, commas, and question marks would all chunk the raw transcription in terms of timing to be sent to the fast assistant.
S33. And so he would get sub sentence level timing.
S34. And then the smart assistant would just get sentence level timing because otherwise we'd need the fast assistant, for example, to decide when to trigger the smart assistant and he'd either forget or do it at the wrong time or whatever.
S35. And so there's really not a better chunking position in the transcription than at each sentence.
S36. And then back to the pacing, sorry, I don't want to use the pseudo properties if you're not familiar what that is, ask the VS Code sidebar.
S37. We should be documenting what the pseudo property system is.
S38. So when I mention it, you guys know what I'm talking about.
S39. Anyway, the pseudo properties in terms of the session logs and the way that this V1 chat works is the wrong way.
S40. It's not a good list.
S41. It's actually a really bad list format.
S42. And so we have lists and we want to be leaning into the list structure.
S43. And so these chats that are being created, each of my prompts... there is a prompt, I'm not sure if our prompt class is being used for V2 and V3.
S44. I think it probably is.
S45. We were talking about having a prompt instance per sentence.
S46. I don't know if that's actually still happening.
S47. We've talked about structuring sentences by ID, that's where that S1 through S2 or S7 or whatever, sentence ID.
S48. I don't know if we want a list of sentences.
S49. I think that synthesis.md, the VS Code mastermind might know about, had some information about what kind of shapes we were looking for.
S50. So, you know, have him look into, you know, well, maybe I 'll stop this transcription and hop back over to that one and talk to him directly.
"""

Output ONLY the Markdown described above (the H1, its H2s, and their bullets), nothing else.
